items.title: Butch Miles interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: It took a long time to get into Duke Ellington’s music... I happened to see the Duke at a jazz festival... So I loved Duke’s music.

ctx.x: Well there’s no disrespect to Mr. Nelson, I just couldn’t stand his playing (sorry about the towel, it’s still dripping, does this come on the microphone, that’s all right we’ll get it later). I started out on a drum set playing the most banal rock ‘n roll, this was in 1959, 1958. And there was really nothing going on in rock ‘n roll exciting or creative, not like a lot of the wonderful, wonderful bands you’ve got now and the great drummers you’ve got now. It was all pretty cut and dried and very boring. But I…
and that got me further and I should say deeper and deeper into that style era of the ‘30’s, and the ‘40’s and the ‘50’s.

items.title: Butch Miles interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 9, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: action-reaction that Duke Ellington was a big fan of. So I just took a page out of his book.

ctx.x: Right. Now I’m going to take a pause for a moment because my connection here needs to go from — I think I need to plug in my — Okay we’re back. So the student that comes in and plays — the first thing they show you is the recreation of a Steve Smith drum solo or a Butch Miles drum solo, and you say, “Very impressive. And now —”

Well the way the I like to try to teach my students with using some of these various methods is that I’ll teach them the methods themselves, the techniques that are in there. Because I’m a big believer in muscle memory, especially with drummers. If you play something and practice something over and over and over and over and over, you know exactly what I mean, sooner or later, believe it or not folks, the muscles will start to retain the memory of the motion that you’re making. And then you stop increasing the…
That begs the question, the relationship between ideas, creative ideas and technique, do you have to have the technique first so that you can then pull off these ideas that you get?
